sections.h2: What records does Washtenaw County hold in its deed office?
sections.html:
Anyone researching land in Washtenaw County ends up at the Register of Deeds. Its files include deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records, along with other real and personal property papers. The register works inside the joint Clerk / Register of Deeds department, and inspection is open to all comers.

The office's main page links to recording rules, record searches and requests, eRecording, a fee schedule and a transfer tax explainer. Copies bought through the online land record search need a login.

Recording finishes a sale, because the buyer is shielded from later claimants only once the deed is on file. Closings usually pass the signed deed to a title company, which can tell you the recording date and supply a recorded copy for your files.

sections.h2: Can Washtenaw County take a deed filed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. Electronic filings come in through vendors approved by the Register of Deeds, a route lenders and title agents rely on. An owner who signs outside a title closing usually files on paper, mailing it or visiting the counter in Ann Arbor.

Read the recording requirements page before you send anything; a paper with layout defects comes back unrecorded. The fee schedule page states what the county charges for each service.

  • Keep the original signed deed in hand until the county accepts it.
  • Ask which payment types the office takes for your kind of filing.
  • Request your recorded deed before listing, so the buyer's title agent has the legal description early.

sections.h2: What do state statutes set for Washtenaw County recording and transfer tax?
sections.html:
Michigan statutes supply the baseline figures for any register of deeds, and Washtenaw's fee schedule page shows how the county applies them. Each charge below is paired with its section; read the text itself at the Michigan Legislature site.

Statutory charges that frame a Washtenaw County deed filing
ChargeRateSection
Placing a paper in the land records$30.00 whatever its length600.2567(1)(a)
Extra instrument within one discharge or assignment$3.00 each600.2567(1)(b)
Record copies$1.00 per sheet600.2567(1)(c)
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00600.2567(1)(d)
County share of transfer tax55 cents per $500 or part of $500 where the county has fewer than 2,000,000 people207.504
State share of transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or part of $500207.525

sections.h2: Who pays transfer tax in a Washtenaw County sale, and what avoids it?
sections.html:
Sellers carry this one. MCL 207.523 makes the grantor liable and sets a 15-day window, running from delivery of the deed, for payment to the county treasurer. Washtenaw's explainer adds a rule that trips people up. Collection is automatic unless the deed qualifies and states the reason on its face.

Any exemption you plan to claim therefore belongs in the document itself. MCL 207.526 lists the categories, including:

  • Spouses who set up or end a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A parent or grandparent deeding to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild.
  • A boundary line fix with no money changing hands.
  • A joint tenancy where one of the co-owners already holds title.
  • A deed delivered through foreclosure or in place of it.

A payer who later learns that an exemption applied can request a refund from the state Treasury department under subsection (4) of the section on liability.

sections.h2: Does a Washtenaw County warranty deed need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
Usually. MCL 211.135 has registers of deeds ask for treasurer certificates whenever a deed or land contract is presented. They disclose tax liens or tax titles and confirm that the five years of tax before the instrument date were paid.

Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excused, as are sheriff's deeds and a few other kinds. A Washtenaw seller using an ordinary warranty deed should plan on the certificate first.

If back tax is owing, the Washtenaw County Treasurer can quote a payoff figure. Settle it by closing and the certificate issues, so the deed can be filed without a stall.

sections.h2: How should a Washtenaw County deed be formatted?
sections.html:
Format rules are in MCL 565.201, and a register must refuse any paper that breaks them. Check these before anyone signs.

  • The first printed line states the single recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • Black ink, white paper of 20-pound weight or heavier, type of at least 10 points.
  • 2 1/2 inches blank above the text on page one and half an inch on every remaining edge.
  • Grantee addresses, with the drafter's name and business address.
  • Any Social Security number cut to its last four digits.
  • An English translation stapled to anything partly in another language.

The office also enrolls people in Fraud Guard alerts, which warn you when a paper is recorded under your name. It is a sensible precaution while a house sits listed or vacant. Two other county pages cover older paperwork: discharging prohibited deed restrictions, such as covenants that discriminated by race or religion, and the Michigan Construction Lien Act, which matters if contractors recently worked on the house.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Washtenaw County?
sections.html:
Michigan's territorial government defined the county in 1822 and organized it in 1826. French traders built the first lasting settlement at Ypsilanti around 1809. The University of Michigan moved to Ann Arbor in 1839, a consolation after the city lost its bid for the state capital, and Eastern Michigan University began as a normal school in Ypsilanti in 1849. Early settlers drained swamps for farms, and parts of the Waterloo Recreation Area still look as they did then. Greek Revival buildings and township names reflect the 1820s and 1830s enthusiasm for Greece.

The university is the largest employer in a July 2020 list, followed by Trinity Health, federal jobs, Ann Arbor Public Schools, the Toyota Technical Center, Faurecia, Eastern Michigan University, IHA Health Services and the State of Michigan. Domino's Pizza, Thomson Reuters and NSF International also make the top fifteen.

The county spans 722 square miles, 706 of them land, and borders Livingston, Oakland, Wayne, Monroe, Lenawee, Jackson and Ingham counties. Ann Arbor is the seat. Chelsea, Dexter, Manchester, Saline, Ypsilanti and the northern slice of Milan are the other cities, with Barton Hills a village and Whitmore Lake a census community. Main roads are I-94, US 23, US 12, M-14, M-17 and M-52, and the county runs 10 parks and a recreation center.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Washtenaw County homes?
sections.html:
Census estimates put Washtenaw County at 370,214 people in 2025 living in 165,103 housing units. Owners occupy 61.6 percent of homes, and the middle owner-occupied value is $374,100, about double Wayne County's. Typical household income is $89,180 and typical gross rent is $1,463. Bachelor's degrees or higher belong to 58.7 percent of adults. Around 79 percent of residents stayed at the same address over the prior year, 13.1 percent were born abroad and the mean commute is 23.5 minutes.

The county counts 8,322 employer establishments with 158,858 jobs for 2023, and health care and social assistance took in about $8.7 billion in 2022. Population density reaches 527 per square mile. Zoning, building permits and assessing belong to local units, so ask the city or township about any open permit before you list.

faqs.q: Does Washtenaw County take electronic deed filings?
faqs.a: Yes. Lenders and title companies commonly file through eRecording vendors that the Register of Deeds has approved.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for transfer tax in a Washtenaw County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. Michigan sets 55 cents for the county plus $3.75 for the state on each $500 of value, and the county treasurer must receive payment within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: Does my Washtenaw County deed have to name a transfer tax exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. According to the county's explainer, the tax is collected unless the instrument is exempt and the exemption appears on the face of the deed, so write out the statutory reason before signing.

faqs.q: What tax paperwork goes with a Washtenaw County warranty deed?
faqs.a: Certificates from the county treasurer showing no tax liens or titles and five prior years of paid taxes. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excused.

faqs.q: Where can I confirm the Washtenaw County recording fee?
faqs.a: Check the Register of Deeds fee schedule page, which covers recording, copies, searches, transfer tax and tax certificates. State law sets the starting recording charge at $30.00 per document.
